chunks: From him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Place the matter of your brother upon its best interpretation until there comes to you what would overwhelm you from him, and do not suppose evil with a speech that comes out from your brother while you can find an interpretation of it regarding goodness.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic principle of good presumption towards others?
ai.summary: This narration, recorded in Al-Kafi, establishes the principle of *husn al-zann* (good presumption) as a cornerstone of social harmony in Shia ethics, urging believers to attribute positive intent to their brothers unless compelling evidence suggests otherwise. It reflects the broader theological emphasis on purifying the heart from suspicion (*khabith al-zann*) to maintain communal unity. The advice to wait for 'what overcomes you' implies a threshold of certainty that justifies shifting from presumption to knowledge, balancing optimism with discernment.
